newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: U.N. bodies appeal for funds for Albania polio.
newsitem.headline: U.N. bodies appeal for funds for Albania polio.

text.p: The World Health Organisation (WHO) and the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) on Wednesday appealed for $1,3 million to fund an emergency vaccination campaign against polio in Albania.

A statement from the WHO said 12 people had died and 78 had been infected so far in an outbreak that started in the country in April but had not yet peaked and was showing sign of spreading to neighbouring countries.

Three cases were reported in July and August in Greece and last week six suspected cases were reported in the largely Albanian-populated Kosovo region of the rump Yugoslavia. Two of these had later been confirmed.

Funds attracted by the new appeal would be used for a vaccination campaign, especially among teenagers and young adults who have been the main victims of the outbreak, to follow up an earlier campaign targetted on children.
It would also be used to improve early detection of new cases, the WHO said.
The statement said public health officials in the region were especially concerned by the potential for large numbers of seasonal migrants to spread the polio virus.
An estimated 700,000 Albanians lived in neighbouring countries, mainly Italy and Greece but also in the rump Yugoslavia and Macedonia, and many moved back and forth to Albania each year, it added.
